docs.title: OpenTransition Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the official documentation for OpenTransition - a transition tracking application specifically designed for transgender people, focusing on photo tracking and milestone management.

docs.title: What is OpenTransition?
docs.text:
OpenTransition is a customized fork of the original TransTracks application, rebranded and repackaged for independent deployment. It helps transgender individuals track their transition journey through photos and milestones, providing a private and secure way to document changes over time.

Built on TransTracks

OpenTransition is based on the excellent work of the original TransTracks developers. We're grateful for their contribution to the transgender community. Learn more about credits and attribution →

docs.title: 📸 Photo Tracking
docs.text: Track your transition with photos organized by different body types (face, body, custom areas). Compare photos side-by-side to see your progress over time.

docs.title: 🎯 Milestone Management
docs.text: Record and celebrate important milestones in your transition journey. Track dates, add descriptions, and associate photos with specific achievements.

docs.title: 🖼️ Gallery View
docs.text: Browse your transition photos in an organized gallery. Filter by date, body type, and milestones to find exactly what you're looking for.

docs.title: 🔒 Privacy & Security
docs.text:
• App lock with PIN or pattern
  • Disguised app icon (train mode)
  • Secure local storage
  • Optional cloud sync with Firebase

docs.title: 🎨 Customization
docs.text:
• Multiple theme options (Pink, Blue, Purple, Green)
  • Flexible photo organization
  • Custom milestone types

docs.title: 💾 Data Management
docs.text:
• Import/Export your data
  • Firebase cloud backup
  • Local Realm database

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text: The Data Layer manages all data models, database operations, and persistence in OpenTransition.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The data layer consists of: - Data Models: Realm objects representing app entities - Database: Realm Kotlin for local storage - Cloud Sync: Firebase Firestore for remote backup - File Storage: Local file system for photos

docs.title: Photo Model
docs.text:
The Photo class represents transition photos stored by users.

File: app/src/main/java/com/shelbeely/opentransition/data/Photo.kt

class Photo : RealmObject {
    @PrimaryKey var id: String = UUID.randomUUID().toString()
    var timestamp: Long = 0L
    var epochDay: Long = 0L
    var filename: String = ""
    var type: Int = TYPE_BODY

    companion object {
        const val TYPE_FACE = 0
        const val TYPE_BODY = 1
        const val TYPE_CUSTOM = 2
    }
}

Key Properties: - id: Unique identifier (UUID) - timestamp: Photo capture time in milliseconds - epochDay: Date as epoch day for grouping - filename: Stored filename on device - type: Photo category (face, body, or custom)

Photo Types: - Face (0): Facial progress photos - Body (1): Full body progress photos - Custom (2): User-defined areas

docs.title: Milestone Model
docs.text:
The Milestone class represents significant events in the transition journey.

File: app/src/main/java/com/shelbeely/opentransition/data/Milestone.kt

class Milestone : RealmObject {
    @PrimaryKey var id: String = UUID.randomUUID().toString()
    var title: String = ""
    var description: String = ""
    var epochDay: Long = 0L
    var timestamp: Long = 0L
}

Key Properties: - id: Unique identifier (UUID) - title: Milestone name - description: Detailed description - epochDay: Date as epoch day - timestamp: Creation time in milliseconds

Common Milestone Examples: - Starting HRT - Name change - Coming out milestones - Medical procedures - Legal document updates

docs.text:
Realm is configured in the Application class and opened throughout the app:

// Open default Realm instance
val realm = Realm.openDefault()

// Always close when done

docs.title: Create (Insert)
docs.text:
val realm = Realm.openDefault()
realm.write {
    val photo = Photo().apply {
        id = UUID.randomUUID().toString()
        timestamp = System.currentTimeMillis()
        filename = "photo_${timestamp}.jpg"
        type = Photo.TYPE_BODY
    }
    copyToRealm(photo, UpdatePolicy.ALL)
}
realm.close()

// Get all photos

    photo?.let {

docs.title: Saving Photos
docs.text:
fun copyPhotoToTempFiles(uri: Uri): String? {
    try {
        val inputStream = contentResolver.openInputStream(uri)
        val filename = "photo_${System.currentTimeMillis()}.jpg"
        val outputFile = FileUtil.getImageFile(filename)

        inputStream?.use { input ->
            FileOutputStream(outputFile).use { output ->
                input.copyTo(output)
            }
        }
        return filename
    } catch (e: Exception) {
        return null
    }
}

docs.title: Deleting Photos
docs.text:
fun deletePhoto(filename: String): Boolean {
    val file = FileUtil.getImageFile(filename)
    return if (file.exists()) {
        file.delete()
    } else false
}

docs.title: Syncing Data
docs.text:
class FirebaseSettingUtil {
    private val firestore = FirebaseFirestore.getInstance()
    private val auth = FirebaseAuth.getInstance()

    fun syncPhotos() {
        val userId = auth.currentUser?.uid ?: return
        val photosRef = firestore.collection("users")
            .document(userId)
            .collection("photos")

        val realm = Realm.openDefault()
        val photos = realm.query<Photo>().find()

        photos.forEach { photo ->
            val photoData = hashMapOf(
                "id" to photo.id,
                "timestamp" to photo.timestamp,
                "epochDay" to photo.epochDay,
                "type" to photo.type
                // Note: Actual photo files stored separately
            )
            photosRef.document(photo.id).set(photoData)
        }
        realm.close()
    }
}

docs.title: Photo Validation

fun validatePhoto(photo: Photo): Boolean {
    return photo.id.isNotEmpty() &&
           photo.filename.isNotEmpty() &&
           photo.timestamp > 0 &&
           photo.type in 0..2
}

fun validateMilestone(milestone: Milestone): Boolean {
    return milestone.id.isNotEmpty() &&
           milestone.title.isNotEmpty() &&
           milestone.timestamp > 0

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: OpenTransition follows a clean architecture pattern with clear separation of concerns across three main layers: Data, Domain, and UI.

│                      UI Layer                           │

│  - MainActivity                                         │
│  - Various Fragments (Home, Gallery, Settings, etc.)   │
│  - ViewBinding for UI                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

│  - AssignPhotosDomain                                   │

                           ↓

docs.title: 1. MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel)
docs.text:
OpenTransition uses a variant of MVVM with a Domain layer:

  • Model: Data classes representing Photos, Milestones, etc.
  • View: XML layouts and Fragments
  • ViewModel: Domain classes that manage UI state and business logic
  • Domain Layer: Acts as a ViewModel but is called "Domain" in this codebase

docs.title: 2. Repository Pattern
docs.text: While not explicitly called repositories, the Domain classes act as repositories: - Abstract data access logic - Provide clean API for UI layer - Handle data transformations - Manage background operations

docs.title: 3. Reactive Programming
docs.text: Uses RxJava 3 for: - Asynchronous operations - Event streams - State management - UI updates

docs.title: 4. Dependency Injection
docs.text:

    val homeDomain = HomeDomain()
    val assignPhotosDomain = AssignPhotosDomain()
    val settingsDomain = SettingsDomain()
    val addEditMilestoneDomain = AddEditMilestoneDomain()
    val editPhotoDomain = EditPhotoDomain()
}

docs.title: Typical User Action Flow
docs.text:
1. User Interaction → Fragment receives input
  2. Fragment → Calls Domain method
  3. Domain → Updates Realm database
  4. Realm → Notifies observers via RxJava
  5. Domain → Emits state updates
  6. Fragment → Updates UI

docs.title: Example: Adding a Photo
docs.text:
// 1. User selects photo in UI (Fragment)
pickMediaLauncher.launch(PickVisualMediaRequest(type))

// 2. MainActivity receives result
pickMediaLauncher = registerForActivityResult(PickMultipleVisualMedia()) { uris ->
    // Navigate to assign photos
    navController.navigate(MainNavDirections.actionGlobalAssignPhotos(...))
}

// 3. AssignPhotosFragment gets data
val args: AssignPhotosFragmentArgs by navArgs()

// 4. Domain processes the request
assignPhotosDomain.addPhotos(photoUris, type, date)

// 5. Domain writes to Realm
realm.write {
    copyToRealm(Photo(...), UpdatePolicy.ALL)
}

// 6. UI observes changes and updates
assignPhotosDomain.state
    .observeOn(RxSchedulers.main())
    .subscribe { state -> updateUI(state) }

docs.title: RxSchedulers
docs.text:
Centralized scheduler management:

object RxSchedulers {
    fun main(): Scheduler = AndroidSchedulers.mainThread()
    fun io(): Scheduler = Schedulers.io()
    fun computation(): Scheduler = Schedulers.computation()
}

docs.title: Threading Rules
docs.text:
• UI updates: Main thread only
  • Database operations: IO thread
  • File operations: IO thread
  • Network calls: IO thread
  • Heavy computations: Computation thread

docs.title: Domain State Pattern
docs.text:
Each Domain class manages its own state:

sealed class HomeState {
    object Loading : HomeState()
    data class Success(val photos: List<Photo>) : HomeState()
    data class Error(val message: String) : HomeState()
}

State is exposed via RxJava observables:

class HomeDomain {
    private val _state = BehaviorSubject.create<HomeState>()
    val state: Observable<HomeState> = _state

    fun loadPhotos() {
        _state.onNext(HomeState.Loading)
        // Load data...
        _state.onNext(HomeState.Success(photos))
    }
}

docs.title: Building Release Version
docs.text:
Release Keystore Required

Building a release version requires a release keystore. For production releases, you need a properly configured keystore with secure credentials.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Release Keystore: Generate or obtain your release keystore
  2. Environment Variables: Set the following:
  3. STORE_PASS: Keystore password
  4. KEY_ALIAS: Key alias
  5. KEY_PASS: Key password
  6. Keystore File: Place at keys/release-keystore.jks

docs.title: Generate a Release Keystore (First Time Only)
docs.text:
# Navigate to keys directory
cd keys

# Generate keystore
keytool -genkey -v -keystore release-keystore.jks \
  -alias opentransition \
  -keyalg RSA \
  -keysize 2048 \
  -validity 10000

Follow the prompts to set passwords and enter your information.

Security Critical

  • Never commit the release keystore to version control
  • Store keystore and passwords securely (use a password manager)
  • Back up your keystore in a secure location
  • Loss of keystore means you cannot update your app on Play Store

docs.title: Build Release APK
docs.text:
Linux/macOSWindows (PowerShell) 
export STORE_PASS="your_store_password"
export KEY_ALIAS="your_key_alias"
export KEY_PASS="your_key_password"

./gradlew assembleRelease

$env:STORE_PASS="your_store_password"
$env:KEY_ALIAS="your_key_alias"
$env:KEY_PASS="your_key_password"

.\gradlew.bat assembleRelease

The signed APK will be at: app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk

docs.title: Build Android App Bundle (AAB)
docs.text:

# Set environment variables (as shown above)
export STORE_PASS="your_store_password"
export KEY_ALIAS="your_key_alias"
export KEY_PASS="your_key_password"

# Build bundle
./gradlew bundleRelease

The AAB will be at: app/build/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab

docs.title: Version Information
docs.text:
Version information is defined in app/build.gradle:

def major = 1
def minor = 3

def getVersionCode = { ->
    def envBuildNumber = System.getenv("BUILD_NUMBER")?.toInteger() ?: 0
    def baseBuildNumber = 25
    return baseBuildNumber + (major * 100) + minor + envBuildNumber
}

def getVersionName = { ->
    return "$major.$minor.${getVersionCode()}"
}
  • Major: Incremented for major releases
  • Minor: Incremented for minor updates
  • Build Number: Auto-incremented in CI/CD (defaults to 0 locally)

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text: This guide walks you through setting up your development environment for OpenTransition.

docs.title: Step 1: Install Android Studio
docs.text:
1. Download Android Studio for your platform
  2. Run the installer and follow the setup wizard
  3. Install the Android SDK and necessary build tools

SDK Setup

During installation, ensure you install:

  • Android SDK Platform 36
  • Android SDK Build-Tools
  • Android Emulator
  • Android SDK Platform-Tools

docs.title: Step 2: Install Java Development Kit (JDK)
docs.text: OpenTransition requires JDK 17.

docs.title: Option 1: Install via Android Studio
docs.text: Android Studio includes a JDK. You can use it by configuring your project to use the embedded JDK.

docs.title: Option 2: Install Separately
docs.text:
WindowsmacOSLinux 
# Download JDK 17 from Oracle or use a package manager
# Then set JAVA_HOME environment variable
setx JAVA_HOME "C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-17"

# Using Homebrew
brew install openjdk@17

# Set JAVA_HOME in your shell profile
echo 'export JAVA_HOME=$(/usr/libexec/java_home -v 17)' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc

# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt update
sudo apt install openjdk-17-jdk

# Set JAVA_HOME
echo 'export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

Verify installation:

java -version
# Should show version 17.x.x

docs.title: Step 3: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/shelbeely/OpenTransition.git
cd OpenTransition

docs.title: Step 4: Set Up Firebase
docs.text: OpenTransition uses Firebase for authentication, cloud storage, analytics, and crash reporting.

docs.title: Create a Firebase Project
docs.text:
1. Go to Firebase Console
  2. Click "Add project" or "Create a project"
  3. Enter a project name (e.g., "OpenTransition Dev")
  4. Follow the setup wizard (Analytics is optional for development)

docs.title: Add Android App to Firebase
docs.text:
1. In the Firebase Console, click "Add app" and select Android
  2. Package name: com.shelbeely.opentransition
  3. App nickname: Optional (e.g., "OpenTransition Android")
  4. Debug signing certificate SHA-1: Optional for development
  5. Click "Register app"

docs.title: Download Configuration File
docs.text:
1. Download the google-services.json file
  2. Place it in the app/ directory of your project: 
    OpenTransition/
└── app/
    └── google-services.json  ← Place it here

Security Note

The google-services.json file contains sensitive API keys and should never be committed to version control. It's already listed in .gitignore.

docs.title: Enable Firebase Services
docs.text:
Enable the following services in your Firebase project:

  1. Authentication
  2. Go to Authentication > Sign-in method
  3. Enable "Email/Password"

  4. Enable "Google" sign-in

  5. Firestore Database

  6. Go to Firestore Database
  7. Click "Create database"
  8. Start in test mode for development

  9. Choose a location close to your users

  10. Crashlytics (Optional for development)

  11. Go to Crashlytics

  12. Click "Enable Crashlytics"

  13. Analytics (Optional for development)

  14. Automatically enabled when you create the project

docs.title: Step 5: Configure Secrets
docs.text:
OpenTransition uses a secrets.properties file for sensitive configuration.

  1. Copy the example file: 

    cp secrets.properties.example secrets.properties

  2. Open secrets.properties and configure the values:

# Firebase AdMob App ID (use test ID for development)
ADS_APP_ID=ca-app-pub-3940256099942544~3347511713

# AdMob Ad Unit IDs (test IDs for development)
ADS_GALLERY_AD_ID=ca-app-pub-3940256099942544/9214589741
ADS_HOME_AD_ID=ca-app-pub-3940256099942544/9214589741
ADS_MILESTONES_AD_ID=ca-app-pub-3940256099942544/9214589741
ADS_SETTINGS_AD_ID=ca-app-pub-3940256099942544/9214589741

# Security salt for PIN/Pattern hashing (generate a random string)
CODE_SALT=your_random_salt_string_here_change_this

Generating CODE_SALT

Generate a secure random string for CODE_SALT:

# Linux/macOS
openssl rand -base64 32

# Or use any random string generator

Production Values

The example values are test/development values. Never use them in production. Get your own AdMob IDs from AdMob Console.

docs.title: Step 6: Open Project in Android Studio
docs.text:
1. Launch Android Studio
  2. Select "Open an Existing Project"
  3. Navigate to the cloned OpenTransition directory
  4. Click "OK"

Android Studio will: - Import the Gradle project - Download dependencies - Index the project files

This may take several minutes on the first run.

docs.title: Step 7: Sync Gradle
docs.text:
Once the project is opened:

  1. Click "Sync Project with Gradle Files" button (or File > Sync Project with Gradle Files)
  2. Wait for the sync to complete
  3. Resolve any errors that appear

Common Sync Issues

  • Missing google-services.json: Ensure the file is in app/ directory
  • Missing secrets.properties: Ensure you copied and configured it
  • SDK not found: Install the required SDK version (36) in SDK Manager

docs.title: Step 8: Configure an Android Virtual Device (AVD)
docs.text:
If you don't have a physical Android device:

  1. Open AVD Manager (Tools > Device Manager)
  2. Click "Create Virtual Device"
  3. Select a device definition (e.g., Pixel 5)
  4. Select a system image (API 34 or higher recommended)
  5. Click "Finish"

docs.text:

  2. Click the "Run" button (green play icon) or press Shift + F10
  3. Wait for the build to complete and the app to launch

  4. You can navigate through the app

docs.title: Full Description
docs.text: OpenTransition is a thoughtfully designed app for transgender individuals to document and track their transition journey through photos and milestones. Keep your progress private, secure, and organized—all in one place.

docs.title: 🌈 Your Journey, Your Privacy
docs.text: OpenTransition puts you in control. Every photo, every milestone, every moment of your journey stays private on your device. With optional cloud backup, app lock, and even a disguised app icon, your transition documentation is truly yours alone.

docs.title: 📸 Visual Progress Tracking
docs.text: Take photos with confidence: - Track different body areas separately (face, body, custom areas) - Compare photos side-by-side to see your changes over time - Organize photos by date automatically - View your journey in a beautiful gallery

docs.title: 🎯 Milestone Celebrations
docs.text: Remember every important moment: - Record significant events (starting HRT, coming out, name changes, etc.) - Add notes and dates to each milestone - Associate photos with specific achievements - Look back and celebrate how far you've come

docs.title: 🔒 Privacy & Security Features
docs.text: Your data is protected: - App Lock: Secure with PIN or pattern - Disguised Mode: Hide the app with a train-themed icon - Local Storage: Data stays on your device by default - Optional Cloud Backup: Sync securely with your Google account when you choose - No Tracking: We don't collect or sell your personal information

docs.title: 🎨 Customizable Experience
docs.text: Make it yours: - Choose from multiple color themes (Pink, Blue, Purple, Green) - Organize photos your way - Create custom milestone types - Dark mode friendly interface

docs.title: 💾 Data You Control
docs.text: Your data, your rules: - Export all your data anytime as a backup file - Import data to restore or move to a new device - Cloud sync is completely optional - Delete everything with one tap if needed

docs.title: 🆓 Free & Open Source
docs.text: OpenTransition is completely free to use with optional ads that support development. It's also open source, meaning the community can review the code, contribute features, and ensure your privacy is respected.

docs.title: ✨ Perfect For:
docs.text:
• Tracking hormone therapy (HRT) progress
  • Documenting facial/body changes
  • Recording important transition milestones
  • Celebrating your journey privately
  • Sharing progress with healthcare providers (optional)

docs.title: 🤝 Made for the Community, by the Community
docs.text:
OpenTransition is a community-maintained fork of TransTracks. We're grateful to the original TransTracks developers for creating this valuable tool for the transgender community. Their foundational work made OpenTransition possible.

This fork is independently maintained and improved by community contributors. Your feedback and suggestions help make the app better for everyone.

Credits: Original app © 2018-2021 TransTracks. OpenTransition fork and enhancements by the community.

Important Notes:

  • This app requires Android 5.0 or higher
  • Camera permission is optional (for taking photos directly in app)
  • Storage permission is needed to import existing photos
  • Internet permission is only used for optional cloud sync and Firebase services
  • The app works completely offline if you choose

Privacy First: We believe your transition journey is deeply personal. That's why OpenTransition is designed with privacy at its core. No forced accounts, no tracking, no selling your data—just a simple, secure tool to help you document your journey on your own terms.

Download OpenTransition today and start documenting your journey with confidence and privacy.

docs.title: What is OpenTransition?
docs.text: OpenTransition is a free, private app designed for transgender individuals to document their transition journey through photos and milestones. It helps you track changes over time, celebrate important moments, and keep everything organized in one secure place.

docs.title: Is OpenTransition really free?
docs.text: Yes! OpenTransition is completely free to use. The app includes optional ads that help support development, but all features are available for free with no subscription required.

docs.title: Is OpenTransition open source?
docs.text:
Yes! OpenTransition is open source software licensed under GPL v3. This means: - The source code is publicly available for review - The community can contribute improvements - You can verify there's no hidden tracking or data collection - It's transparent about what it does with your data

Visit our GitHub: https://github.com/shelbeely/OpenTransition

docs.title: Where is my data stored?
docs.text: By default, all your photos and data are stored locally on your device. Nothing is uploaded to the internet unless you choose to enable cloud backup.

docs.title: Do I need to create an account?
docs.text: No! You can use OpenTransition completely without creating any account. An account is only needed if you want to use the optional cloud backup feature.

docs.title: Can you see my photos?
docs.text: Absolutely not. Your photos stay on your device. We have no access to your photos, data, or personal information. Even if you use cloud backup, your data is stored in your own Google Firebase account, not ours.

docs.title: Is my data tracked or sold?
docs.text: No. OpenTransition does not: - Track your usage (Analytics is opt-in only) - Sell your data - Share your information with third parties - Collect personal information beyond what's needed for optional features

docs.title: How secure is the app lock?
docs.text: The app lock uses industry-standard hashing to store your PIN or pattern securely. Your actual PIN/pattern is never stored—only a hashed version is saved, making it very difficult for anyone to access your data without your code.

docs.title: What is "Train Mode"?
docs.text: Train Mode is a disguise feature that changes the app icon to look like a train/railway app. This provides an extra layer of privacy by making the app less obviously related to transgender transition tracking. Perfect for situations where you want to keep your transition private.

docs.title: What's the difference between Face, Body, and Custom photo types?
docs.text:
• Face: For tracking facial changes (great for seeing HRT effects on your face)
  • Body: For full-body progress photos
  • Custom: For any specific area you want to track separately (hands, legs, hair, etc.)

You can use all three types to organize your photos in whatever way makes sense for your journey.

docs.title: Can I import photos I've already taken?
docs.text: Yes! You can import existing photos from your device: 1. Tap the ➕ button 2. Select "Import Photos" 3. Choose the photos you want to add 4. Select the date they were taken 5. Choose the photo type

docs.title: How do I compare photos side-by-side?
docs.text:
1. Open the Gallery
  2. Tap any photo to view it full screen
  3. Swipe left or right to see other photos
  4. Photos are automatically sorted by date for easy comparison

docs.title: Can I delete photos?
docs.text:
Yes! To delete a photo: 1. Open the photo in full screen 2. Tap the trash/delete icon 3. Confirm deletion

Note: Deleted photos are permanently removed and cannot be recovered unless you have a backup.

docs.title: How many photos can I store?
docs.text: There's no hard limit on the number of photos. The only limit is your device's available storage space. We recommend keeping high-quality photos and backing up regularly.

docs.title: How do I backup my data?
docs.text:
Local Backup (Recommended): 1. Go to Settings → Backup & Sync 2. Tap "Export Data" 3. Save the .ttbackup file somewhere safe (Google Drive, computer, external drive)

Cloud Backup (Optional): 1. Go to Settings → Backup & Sync 2. Sign in with Google 3. Enable Cloud Sync 4. Your data automatically backs up to your Firebase account

docs.title: What's included in a backup?
docs.text: A backup includes: - All your photos - All milestones and their details - App settings (theme, preferences, etc.) - Everything needed to restore your data completely

docs.title: How do I restore from a backup?
docs.text:
1. Locate your .ttbackup file
  2. Tap it to open with OpenTransition
  3. Confirm you want to import the data
  4. Wait for the import to complete

The app will import all photos, milestones, and settings from the backup.

docs.title: Can I transfer my data to a new phone?
docs.text:
Yes! Here's how:

On your old phone: 1. Create a backup (Export Data) 2. Save the .ttbackup file to cloud storage or email it to yourself

On your new phone: 1. Install OpenTransition 2. Download the backup file 3. Open the .ttbackup file with OpenTransition 4. Import completes!

docs.title: What happens if I lose my phone?
docs.text: If you have a backup (local or cloud), you can restore everything on a new device. If you don't have a backup, unfortunately your data cannot be recovered. This is why regular backups are so important!

docs.title: What is Firebase?
docs.text: Firebase is Google's cloud platform that powers the optional cloud backup feature. When you enable cloud sync, your data is stored in a Firebase database linked to your Google account.

docs.title: Do I need to use cloud sync?
docs.text: No! Cloud sync is completely optional. The app works perfectly fine without it, storing everything locally on your device.

docs.title: Is cloud sync secure?
docs.text: Yes. Firebase uses industry-standard encryption and security. Your data is: - Encrypted in transit - Stored securely in Google's cloud infrastructure - Only accessible through your Google account - Protected by Google's security measures

docs.title: Does cloud sync cost money?
docs.text: No. The free tier of Firebase is more than enough for personal use of OpenTransition. You won't incur any charges.

docs.title: How do I disable cloud sync?
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings → Backup & Sync
  2. Tap "Disable Cloud Sync"
  3. Optionally delete cloud data
  4. Sign out of Google account

Your local data remains untouched.

docs.title: The app keeps crashing. What should I do?
docs.text: Try these steps: 1. Force close the app and restart it 2. Clear the app cache (Settings → Apps → OpenTransition → Clear Cache) 3. Ensure you have the latest version from Play Store 4. If problem persists, report it on GitHub with details about when it crashes

docs.title: Photos aren't loading properly
docs.text:
This might be due to: - Corrupted image files - Low storage space on device - Permission issues

Try: 1. Check your device has adequate storage 2. Verify photo permissions are granted 3. Restart the app 4. If problem continues, try reimporting the photos

docs.title: I forgot my app lock PIN/pattern
docs.text:
Unfortunately, if you forget your PIN or pattern, there's no way to recover it (this is by design for security). Your options: 1. Uninstall and reinstall the app (you'll lose data unless you have a backup) 2. If you have a backup from before the lock was set, restore from it

Tip: Write down your PIN/pattern and store it somewhere safe!

docs.title: Cloud sync isn't working
docs.text: Check these: - You're signed into a Google account - You have an internet connection - Cloud sync is enabled in settings - Try signing out and back in - Check Firebase console for any issues

docs.title: Import failed with errors
docs.text: If import fails: - Verify the .ttbackup file isn't corrupted - Ensure you have enough storage space - Check all required permissions are granted - Try importing on a different device

docs.title: Can I change the theme?
docs.text: Yes! Go to Settings → Appearance and choose from: - Pink (default) - Blue - Purple - Green

docs.title: Can I add my own milestone types?
docs.text: Currently, milestones are free-form. You can type any title and description you want. Future versions may add predefined milestone types.

docs.title: Does the app remind me to take photos?
docs.text: Yes! Enable photo reminders in Settings → Notifications. You can choose how often you want to be reminded (weekly, bi-weekly, monthly).

docs.title: Can I share photos with my doctor?
docs.text:
Yes. You can: 1. Export individual photos from the gallery 2. Share them via any app (email, messaging, etc.) 3. Show your phone screen directly during appointments

The app doesn't have built-in sharing to protect your privacy, but you can manually share what you choose.

docs.title: Can I add notes to photos?
docs.text: Currently, photos don't have individual note fields. However, you can: - Add photos to specific dates - Link photos to milestones (which have description fields) - Use milestone descriptions as notes for specific time periods

docs.title: How do I update the app?
docs.text:
OpenTransition updates through the Google Play Store: 1. Open Play Store 2. Go to "My apps & games" 3. Find OpenTransition 4. Tap "Update"

Or enable auto-updates for the app in Play Store settings.

docs.text: Absolutely! We welcome suggestions: 1. Visit GitHub Issues 2. Search to see if it's already suggested 3. If not, create a new feature request 4. Describe what you'd like and why it would be helpful

docs.title: How can I contribute?
docs.text: There are many ways to help: - Report bugs you encounter - Suggest features you'd like - Help improve documentation - Contribute code (if you're a developer) - Share the app with others who might find it useful - Leave a review on the Play Store

docs.text: Currently, the main community space is GitHub. A Discord or forum may be created in the future based on community interest.

docs.title: I'm struggling with my transition. Can the app help?
docs.text:
OpenTransition is a tool for tracking your journey, but it's not a substitute for professional support. If you're struggling, please reach out to:

  • Trans Lifeline: 1-877-565-8860 (US), 1-877-330-6366 (Canada)
  • Trevor Project: 1-866-488-7386 or text START to 678678
  • PFLAG: pflag.org for family support
  • Your healthcare provider or therapist

docs.title: The app is making me focus too much on appearance
docs.text:
If tracking photos becomes unhealthy or obsessive, it's okay to: - Take a break from the app - Reduce photo frequency - Focus on milestone achievements instead of physical changes - Talk to a therapist about your feelings

Your mental health is more important than any tracking app.

docs.title: Getting Started with OpenTransition
docs.text: Welcome to OpenTransition! This guide will help you set up and start using the app to track your transition journey.

docs.title: What is OpenTransition?
docs.text: OpenTransition is a free, private app designed specifically for transgender individuals to document their transition through photos and milestones. Think of it as your personal, secure transition diary that lives on your phone.

docs.title: Why Use OpenTransition?
docs.text: ✅ Private & Secure - Your photos and data stay on your device ✅ Easy to Use - Simple interface designed for everyone ✅ Free - No subscription fees, no hidden costs ✅ Your Data - Export, backup, or delete anytime ✅ Optional Cloud Sync - Backup to your Google account if you want

docs.title: 1. Download & Install
docs.text: Download OpenTransition from the Google Play Store and install it on your Android device (requires Android 5.0 or higher).

docs.title: 2. Open the App
docs.text: When you first open OpenTransition, you'll see the home screen. No account required to start using the app!

docs.title: 3. Grant Permissions (Optional)
docs.text:
The app may ask for permissions:

  • Camera: To take photos directly in the app (you can skip this and import photos instead)
  • Storage/Photos: To import existing photos from your device
  • Notifications: To remind you to take progress photos (optional)

Permissions are Optional

You can use the app without granting permissions. Just import photos manually when you want to add them.

docs.title: Home Screen
docs.text: The home screen shows: - Your most recent photos - Upcoming milestones - Quick access to add photos or milestones - Your transition timeline

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
The app has four main sections:

  1. Home 🏠 - Overview and recent activity
  2. Gallery 🖼️ - Browse all your photos
  3. Milestones 🎯 - Track important events
  4. Settings ⚙️ - Customize and configure the app

docs.title: Main Actions
docs.text: ➕ Add Button - Tap the plus button to: - Take a new photo - Import existing photos - Add a milestone - Create a note

docs.title: Option 1: Take a Photo with Camera
docs.text:
1. Tap the ➕ button
  2. Select Take Photo
  3. Choose photo type (Face, Body, or Custom)
  4. Take your photo
  5. Select the date (defaults to today)
  6. Save!

docs.title: Option 2: Import Existing Photos
docs.text:
1. Tap the ➕ button
  2. Select Import Photos
  3. Choose photo type (Face, Body, or Custom)
  4. Select one or more photos from your device
  5. Choose the date for each photo
  6. Save!

Photo Types

  • Face: For facial progress (great for tracking HRT facial changes)
  • Body: For full body progress photos
  • Custom: For specific areas you want to track separately

docs.title: Adding Your First Milestone
docs.text:
Milestones help you remember important events in your transition.

  1. Tap the ➕ button
  2. Select Add Milestone
  3. Enter a title (e.g., "Started HRT", "First therapy session", "Changed name legally")
  4. Add details (optional)
  5. Set the date
  6. Save!

docs.title: Common Milestones to Track
docs.text:
• 🏥 Medical events (HRT start date, surgeries, doctor appointments)
  • 📝 Legal changes (name change, gender marker changes)
  • 💬 Social milestones (coming out events, first day presenting)
  • 🎉 Personal celebrations (first voice pass, first time using public restroom)

docs.title: Gallery View
docs.text:
1. Tap Gallery in the bottom navigation
  2. Browse all your photos organized by date
  3. Filter by photo type (Face, Body, Custom)
  4. Tap any photo to view it full screen

docs.title: Compare Photos
docs.text:
1. Open any photo in gallery
  2. Swipe left or right to see other photos
  3. Use the comparison view to see changes over time
  4. Photos are automatically organized by date for easy comparison

docs.title: Timeline View
docs.text:
1. View your milestones in chronological order
  2. See which photos are associated with milestones
  3. Track your journey month by month

docs.title: Photo Organization Tips
docs.text:
• Take photos in similar lighting for better comparison
  • Use the same angle and distance each time
  • Take photos on a regular schedule (weekly, monthly, etc.)
  • Label custom areas clearly (e.g., "Hands", "Legs", "Hair")

docs.title: Milestone Organization Tips
docs.text:
• Be specific with milestone titles
  • Add notes about how you felt or what happened
  • Include relevant medical information (dosages, medications)
  • Link photos to milestones when appropriate

docs.title: Using App Lock
docs.text:
Protect your photos with a PIN or pattern:

  1. Go to Settings
  2. Tap Security
  3. Enable App Lock
  4. Choose PIN or Pattern
  5. Set your code

Now the app will lock when you close it!

docs.title: Disguised Mode (Train Icon)
docs.text:
Want extra privacy? Enable "Train Mode":

  1. Go to Settings
  2. Tap Security
  3. Enable Train Mode
  4. The app icon changes to look like a train app

Perfect for keeping your transition journey private!

docs.title: Cloud Backup (Optional)
docs.text:
You can optionally backup your data to Google:

  1. Go to Settings
  2. Tap Backup & Sync
  3. Sign in with Google
  4. Enable Cloud Sync

Your data will now backup automatically!

Backup is Optional

You don't need to create an account or use cloud backup. The app works perfectly fine storing everything locally on your device.

docs.title: Local Backup (Recommended)
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings
  2. Tap Backup & Sync
  3. Tap Export Data
  4. Choose where to save the backup file
  5. Keep this file safe!

This creates a .ttbackup file containing all your photos and data.

docs.title: Restoring from Backup
docs.text:
1. Open OpenTransition
  2. Find your .ttbackup file
  3. Tap the file to open it with OpenTransition
  4. Confirm you want to import
  5. Wait for import to complete

Regular Backups

We recommend creating a backup monthly and storing it in a safe place (like Google Drive, Dropbox, or an external drive).

  3. Choose your favorite color theme:
  4. Pink (default)

  3. Enable Photo Reminders
  4. Choose frequency (weekly, bi-weekly, monthly)
